name: MarketScalping Master Roadmap
description: Project planning artifact for the MarketScalping program. This is a planning authority only and does not mutate runtime workflow state.

stages.title: STEP 6 — Financial-State Architecture
stages.description: Establish the authoritative financial state model, startup recovery, and fail-closed reconciliation contract without changing live trading authority.
exit_criteria: Account ledger identified as authority
PositionManager treated as derived projection
Startup recovery is fail-closed and deterministic
Execution journal is evidence-only
stages.notes: Step 6 is complete only when the financial authority model and recovery gate are validated and remain isolated from live-trading execution.

stages.title: 6A — Financial-State Architecture Investigation
stages.description: Audit the current architecture and establish the authority model for accounting, execution, and position state.
exit_criteria: Execution, accounting, and position responsibilities are explicit
PositionManager is not financial authority
AccountingEngine is identified as authoritative ledger
stages.notes: This milestone is already completed in the repo and is the basis for the downstream financial-state contract.

stages.title: 6B — Financial-State Authority
stages.description: Convert the financial authority design into explicit recovery and reconciliation responsibilities.
exit_criteria: Accounting state is recovered before market-event processing
Position projection is rebuilt from accounting state
Divergence blocks startup instead of silently continuing
stages.notes: This milestone is already completed in the repo and is the recovered authority contract.

stages.title: 6C — Financial-State-Aware Risk
stages.description: Define the risk architecture that is aware of financial state, exposure, position, and loss controls before executing any risk-sensitive behavior.
exit_criteria: Risk state contract is defined
Risk gate boundaries are explicit
Financial state is available to pre-commit risk checks
stages.notes: The Stage 6 gate is not considered closed until all 6C sub-stages complete and exit criteria are satisfied.

stages.title: 6C.1 — Risk Architecture Investigation
stages.description: Investigate the risk-state design, exposure model, and execution permission boundaries required before implementing production risk logic.
exit_criteria: Current gap between strategy and financial-state risk is explicit
Required risk contracts are enumerated
Implementation plan is created without implementing risk logic
stages.notes: This is the next planned milestone and is currently eligible to proceed after Step 6 authority foundations are recognized as satisfied.

stages.title: 6C.2 — Risk State Contract
stages.description: Define the explicit risk-state contract and request/response data model required for gating decisions.
exit_criteria: Risk contract is precise
No financial authority is delegated to RiskEngine
Risk gating remains pre-commit only
stages.notes: This milestone is blocked until 6C.1 exits successfully.

stages.title: 6C.3 — Position / Exposure Limits
stages.description: Define position, exposure, and concentration limits as explicit policy constraints instead of ad-hoc calculations.
exit_criteria: Position exposure limits are explicit
Exposure checks are testable
No trade can bypass position limits
stages.notes: Deferred until the risk-state contract is validated.

stages.title: 6C.4 — Risk-per-Trade
stages.description: Specify the per-trade risk budget, position sizing, and acceptance criteria for single-trade exposure.
exit_criteria: Maximum per-trade risk is explicit
Per-trade risk can be reproduced in validation
No trade is accepted without a risk gate decision
stages.notes: Requires prior exposure-limit definition.

stages.title: 6C.5 — Loss Controls
stages.description: Specify daily, session, and drawdown-based loss controls that are enforced before execution proceeds.
exit_criteria: Loss controls are explicit and testable
No trade can bypass daily drawdown constraints
Human intervention remains required for defined escalation paths
stages.notes: Used to support the fail-safe architecture before any live-trading stage.

stages.title: 6C.6 — Risk Gate Integration
stages.description: Integrate the risk gate into the execution-precondition path without granting RiskEngine financial authority.
required_evidence: risk gate integrated with execution boundary
exit_criteria: Risk gate is enforced before execution acceptance
Execution is still evidence-only relative to accounting
No risk component mutates accounting state
stages.notes: This is integration only; it must not enable live trading.

stages.title: 6C.7 — Risk Validation
stages.description: Validate the risk logic against simulated historical conditions and confirm fail-safe behavior before moving into later stages.
exit_criteria: Risk logic is validated under representative historical stress
Safety and QA evidence is recorded
Risk gate is proven to block unsafe execution paths
stages.notes: This is the final gate for closing Step 6.

stages.title: STEP 7 — Historical Data / Replay
stages.description: Build and validate the historical-data pipeline, canonical schemas, and deterministic replay layer required for reproducible strategy and risk evaluation.
exit_criteria: Raw and canonical data contracts are valid
Replay is deterministic and repeatable
No live exchange path is present in the historical-data pipeline
stages.notes: Step 7 is not eligible until Step 6 is closed under its exit criteria.

stages.title: 7.1 — Historical Data Contract / Canonical Schema
stages.description: Define the canonical normalized data contract, raw-vs-normalized boundaries, and required fields for replay and backtesting.
exit_criteria: Every field is explicitly explained
Replay input matches canonical contract
Malformed or missing data is rejected deterministically
stages.notes: Requires Step 6 authority model to be closed.

stages.title: 7.2 — Collector Integrity
stages.description: Validate the collector pipeline for duplicates, ordering, pagination, malformed records, rate-limit handling, and incomplete windows.
exit_criteria: Collector rejects malformed inputs
No duplicate records are silently accepted
Incomplete windows are explicitly reported
stages.notes: Depends on the canonical data contract.

stages.title: 7.3 — Raw → Validated → Canonical Dataset Flow
stages.description: Define the explicit pipeline from raw exchange data to validated canonical replay input with deterministic checks at each handoff.
exit_criteria: Each dataset stage is identifiable
Validation rules are deterministically applied
Data quality issues are reported without inventing missing values
stages.notes: Flow validation happens after collector integrity is proven.

stages.title: 7.4 — Replay Determinism and Realism
stages.description: Prove that replay can reproduce the same historical event order, timestamps, and market conditions while remaining realistic to the current simulation model.
exit_criteria: Replay output is reproducible
Timestamps and ordering are preserved
No live WebSocket or live trading path is introduced
stages.notes: Replay realism is validated only after the dataset path is defined and stable.

stages.title: STEP 8 — Backtesting Engine
stages.description: Implement a deterministic backtesting layer that simulates execution, fees, slippage, fill behavior, and performance metrics without compromising risk or accounting authority.
exit_criteria: Backtest can reproduce historical behavior
Execution costs are included
Metrics are auditable and reproducible
stages.notes: Backtesting depends on Step 7 replay validity.

stages.title: 8.1 — Backtest Architecture
stages.description: Define the backtest architecture, event flow, and simulation boundaries for strategy and risk evaluation.
exit_criteria: Backtest structure is documented and testable
Historical replay is the canonical input source
Risk and accounting boundaries are preserved
stages.notes: Defines the simulation boundary for later strategy validation.

stages.title: 8.2 — Strategy and Risk Integration
stages.description: Integrate strategy, risk, and execution assumptions into the backtest engine without granting any execution component financial authority.
exit_criteria: Strategy and risk decisions are simulated as explicit state transitions
Execution is simulated with realistic constraints
Accounting remains authoritative
stages.notes: This is a simulation-only integration layer.

stages.title: 8.3 — Fees, Spread, Slippage, Latency, and Fill Behavior
stages.description: Model execution realism, including fees, spread, slippage, latency, partial fills, failed orders, and minimum-order constraints.
exit_criteria: The backtest includes cost and execution realism
Failed orders and partial fills are represented
Results are explainable and reproducible
stages.notes: Cost realism is mandatory before any strategy is considered credible.

stages.title: 8.4 — Backtest Outputs and Performance Metrics
stages.description: Generate auditable output for equity curves, trade ledger, drawdown, and summary metrics required for robust strategy validation.
exit_criteria: Outputs are reproducible
No lookahead or leakage is present
Metrics explain the outcome under realistic cost assumptions
stages.notes: This stage closes the backtesting engine planning work.

stages.title: STEP 9 — Strategy Validation
stages.description: Validate candidate trading strategies under realistic historical and cost-aware conditions before any paper-trading or live deployment is considered. Validation must separate development, validation, and out-of-sample evaluation and must treat a failed strategy as valid research evidence rather than as a hidden success criterion.
exit_criteria: Development, validation, and out-of-sample data are strictly separated with no leakage between them
The strategy survives walk-forward validation and robustness testing under representative conditions
Parameter sensitivity is reported and the strategy is not accepted on a single favorable configuration
Statistical confidence or statistical validity is documented when making performance claims
A strategy that fails validation is recorded as a valid research outcome and cannot be treated as success simply because a profitable backtest existed
A strategy is only considered valid if the defined validation process is passed with objective evidence and not by profit narrative alone
stages.notes: The underlying rule is: profitable backtest alone does not imply successful strategy validation. The strategy must survive the validation process with evidence and remain valid even when it fails.

stages.title: 9.1 — Baseline Strategies and Benchmarking
stages.description: Establish baseline strategies, no-trade baselines, and benchmark comparisons before evaluating candidate strategy improvements. Baselines must be used as a control against claims of improvement and to make failed strategy outcomes meaningful.
exit_criteria: A strategy is judged relative to meaningful baselines and not by isolated performance claims
No false claims are made without comparison to a robust baseline
The strategy is required to beat or justify its baseline under valid evaluation criteria
Research can explicitly fail without being treated as success and without hiding the failure behind a single profitable backtest
stages.notes: Benchmarking is required before model tuning or strategy selection.

stages.title: 9.2 — Walk-Forward and Robustness Testing
stages.description: Evaluate the strategy with time-series aware validation, walk-forward splits, regime analysis, robustness testing, parameter sensitivity, and statistical validity under varying market conditions. The result must be able to reject the strategy when it fails, without treating that rejection as a defect in the process.
exit_criteria: Performance is not overfit to the same window and survives walk-forward validation
Regime dependency and robustness are analyzed under varying conditions
Parameter sensitivity is measurable and documented
Statistical confidence or statistical validity is reported before claiming strategy superiority
The strategy may fail validation legitimately and that failed outcome is treated as valid research evidence
A strategy is not promoted beyond research without passing the defined validation process with objective evidence
stages.notes: This stage is essential before paper trading or model selection. Failure is an acceptable research result when it is evidenced and explicit.

stages.title: STEP 10 — Paper Trading
stages.description: Operate the strategy in a real-time paper-trading environment with real market data and realistic execution assumptions while preserving the fail-safe architecture and accounting authority model. Paper trading must include a sufficient operating period to observe event flow, failure modes, and divergence under realistic conditions before any live-money stage is considered.
exit_criteria: Paper trading remains active for a sufficient longitudinal observation period to capture normal and abnormal market behavior
Paper-trading outcomes are compared against the backtest and explained when they diverge due to latency, spread, data quality, stale inputs, or execution assumptions

WebSocket disconnects, stale-data handling, API failures, process restarts, accounting recovery, corrupted-state handling, duplicate-event handling, and state-divergence detection are all tested and documented
Accounting, risk, and monitoring remain fail-closed under these operational conditions
No live trading permission or real order placement occurs during this stage
stages.notes: Paper trading is a simulation-grade operational rehearsal, not a live-money stage. It must be observed long enough to reveal operational realities and failure modes.

stages.title: 10.1 — Real-Time Market Data and Execution Simulation
stages.description: Use real-time market data and deterministic execution assumptions in a paper environment with realistic latency, stale-data detection, restart handling, failure recovery, and event integrity guarantees.
exit_criteria: Market data and execution remain deterministic under failure conditions
WebSocket disconnects, stale data, and API failures are detected and handled without silent divergence
Process restart and accounting recovery are tested and the system does not silently continue with corrupted state
Duplicate or corrupted events are detected and reconciled
State divergence is observable and blocks unsafe continuation
Account reconciliation remains intact under operational risk conditions
stages.notes: Depends on strategy validation and the stable risk stack. Failure handling is part of the paper-trading acceptance criteria, not an afterthought.

stages.title: 10.2 — Paper-vs-Backtest Comparison
stages.description: Compare paper-trading outcomes with historical backtest results and identify divergence caused by latency, spread, data quality, execution assumptions, or operational conditions. The objective is to prove the real-time operation matches the modeled assumptions before live trading is considered.
exit_criteria: Differences are explained and attributable to real-world operating conditions or model assumptions
No unrecognized divergence remains after a sufficient observation period
A strategy is not promoted without observed realism and a documented explanation of any live-vs-paper gap
The paper-trading process is demonstrably representative of the validated strategy and operational constraints
stages.notes: Required to prove the paper-trading layer is operationally meaningful and can reveal execution reality before a live-money stage.

stages.title: STEP 11 — ML / AI Decision Layer
stages.description: Introduce an ML or AI decision layer only after deterministic strategy behavior and risk constraints are proven, while preserving the risk-engine authority boundary. ML/AI is allowed only as a decision-support layer and must demonstrate measurable incremental value after fees, slippage, and other relevant costs. If no measurable improvement is shown, the model must be rejected or deferred.
exit_criteria: A precise ML prediction target is defined, measured, and auditable
Feature leakage is prevented by design and is explicitly validated
Out-of-sample and walk-forward evidence are used for model selection and not just in-sample performance
The model is evaluated after fees, slippage, and relevant operational costs; measurable incremental value is required before production consideration
Market-regime analysis is included where the decision target is regime-dependent
LLM usage is explicitly bounded to research, analysis, or non-latency-critical tasks and is never part of the per-tick latency-critical decision path
ML/AI must never bypass RiskEngine and must remain a decision-support capability and not an execution authority
ML/AI provides no measurable improvement is explicitly allowed as a valid outcome requiring rejection or deferral of the ML layer
stages.notes: AI/ML may influence strategy decisions only under the same authority and risk constraints as deterministic logic. If it does not demonstrate measurable gain after real costs, it must not be forced into production.

stages.title: 11.1 — Prediction Target and Feature Research
stages.description: Define the prediction target, features, regime analysis, leakage controls, and research architecture required for any ML or AI model under consideration. The model must be assessed against the real decision problem, not a convenient surrogate that hides leakage or ignores cost.
exit_criteria: The feature target is specific, measurable, and relevant to the execution decision
Leakage is prevented by construction and by explicit validation review
Candidate model features are evidence-based and regime-aware where applicable
The evaluation target does not assume a profitable result without cost-aware validation
stages.notes: ML only after a deterministic strategy foundation exists and only when the target and feature design are defensible.

stages.title: 11.2 — Simple Baseline Model and OOS Evaluation
stages.description: Compare a simple baseline model against more complex alternatives using walk-forward and out-of-sample evaluation, with cost-aware scoring and a clear decision rule for rejection or deferral when the AI layer provides no measurable improvement.
exit_criteria: The model is proven to beat the baseline only under valid evaluation with explicit out-of-sample and walk-forward checks
Model decisions remain consistent with risk gates and real operational constraints
LLMs are not used in the real-time trading path and remain outside the latency-critical decision loop
A model that provides no measurable improvement after fees and slippage is rejected or deferred rather than forced into production
The evidence must support either model acceptance or explicit rejection of the ML layer
stages.notes: The ML path remains research-oriented and deterministic. Measurable edge after real costs is required for continued advancement.

stages.title: STEP 12 — Observability / Monitoring
stages.description: Create structured observability, auditability, and alerting from market data, strategy, risk, execution, accounting, recovery, and operational health. The system must be able to reconstruct a decision path and its financial consequence from logs, metrics, and alerts, end-to-end from Market → Feature → Strategy → Risk → Execution → Accounting.
exit_criteria: System metrics and trading metrics are emitted for the major runtime stages and support health assessment
Structured logs are captured for Market, Feature, Strategy, Risk, Execution, and Accounting events
Alerts include recovery-blocked, emergency-stop, abnormal-loss, state-divergence, and unexpected-execution conditions
Operational health is visible across all major stages and state divergence is detectable and auditable
Control Room and alerting support safe operation and human response
Sufficient evidence exists to reconstruct the path from a market signal to a strategy decision, risk decision, execution, and resulting accounting effect
stages.notes: Monitoring is a safety and control layer, not a bypass around risk or accounting authority. It must provide enough evidence to reconstruct decisions and financial impact.

stages.title: 12.1 — Structured Logs and Event Auditing
stages.description: Instrument the system with structured logs covering market data, features, strategy, risk, execution, accounting, recovery, and failures. Logs must support end-to-end reconstruction of the decision and financial effect at each stage.
exit_criteria: Every major component emits auditable signals that can be correlated across the pipeline
State changes are visible and attributable from Market to Feature to Strategy to Risk to Execution to Accounting
Operational incidents can be diagnosed without guessing, including divergence and blocked recovery
A decision can be reconstructed with sufficient evidence to explain the financial effect and the exact runtime reason for the outcome
stages.notes: Support is required for all later operational stages and for incident investigation and auditability.

stages.title: STEP 13 — Live-Trading Safety Architecture
stages.description: Define the read-only market-data boundary, API permissions, kill switch, and capital safeguards required before any controlled live-money trial is considered. This stage remains architecture and safety validation only; it must not enable live trading.
exit_criteria: Strict paper/live separation is explicit and enforced
READ + TRADE API permissions are documented and no withdrawal path exists
Hard capital limit, hard position limit, hard per-trade risk limit, daily loss limit, and maximum open positions are defined
API or network failure results in no new trade being created, and an independent emergency kill switch can stop execution
Production deployment controls are explicit, and human approval remains required before any live activation
This stage creates safety architecture only and does not enable live trading
stages.notes: This is the first explicit live-money architecture stage and still does not perform live trading. The objective is explicit safety validation and approval gating.

stages.title: 13.1 — API Boundary and Permission Model
stages.description: Define the live exchange boundary, API permissions, and controls that ensure read-only market data, trade support, no-withdrawal behavior, and fail-safe production boundaries.
exit_criteria: Permissions are restricted, auditable, and separated from any withdrawal path
No withdrawal path exists and live operational access is bounded by explicit hard limits
Trade and market access remain intentionally bounded and fail-safe under API or network failure
Independent emergency kill switch and human approval gate are the only approved activation path to live operation
The production controls explicitly prevent unsafe live activation without review
stages.notes: Order placement and withdrawal permissions are denied by design. Live activation remains blocked until explicit human approval and safety evidence exist.

stages.title: STEP 14 — ~€10 Controlled Live Test
stages.description: Run a minimal, controlled live-money test with hard limits and explicit human approval, treating the objective as system validation and operational safety rather than profit generation. The first live test exists to prove the real-money pipeline behaves as designed, not to maximize profit.
exit_criteria: Preflight checklist is completed with evidence and human approval before activation
Capital is limited to approximately €10 and is spot-only with no leverage
Strict risk limits are enforced, including daily loss, position, and per-trade risk guardrails
Paper-vs-live comparison is performed and actual fills, fees, spread, slippage, and latency are measured against the simulated assumptions
Unexpected execution, state divergence, abnormal loss, and telemetry failure conditions are actively monitored
Automatic kill conditions remain active throughout the test and human STOP/CONTINUE decisions remain active for the full trial
The primary objective is to prove the real-money pipeline behaves as designed rather than to maximize profit
stages.notes: The purpose is validation and operational safety, not maximizing profit. Any evidence of a breaching or diverging live path blocks continuation.

stages.title: 14.1 — Preflight and Pre-Launch Validation
stages.description: Verify historical validity, paper-trading comparison, observability, and safety checks before any live-money trading begins. This is the explicit launch gate for the first real-money test.
exit_criteria: No unverified risk path remains before live activation
Operational telemetry, alerts, and observability are functioning and auditable
Human approval is required before launch and documented in evidence
Actual live behavior is expected to match the validated risk and execution model; any unresolved discrepancy blocks activation
The first live test begins only after all preflight safety checks and comparison evidence are complete
stages.notes: This is the final gate prior to live-money activation and must produce evidence, not assumptions.

stages.title: STEP 15 — Controlled Scaling
stages.description: Increase capital only in controlled increments, requiring evidence of stability and human approval at each step. Capital growth is a controlled operational decision, not an automatic recovery mechanism for losses.
exit_criteria: Each scale-up is evidence-based and reviewed with explicit human approval
Capital growth is controlled and staged rather than automatic
Performance, risk, stability, and operations remain within approved limits before any increase
No automatic scaling compensates for performance deterioration or losses
The system must demonstrate continued stability and risk control before any additional capital increases are approved
stages.notes: Illustrative capital stages are €10 → €12–15 → €20 → €25 → €40 → ≤€50, with human approval required at each step. Scale-up is evidence-driven and human-controlled.

stages.title: 15.1 — Controlled Capital Increases
stages.description: Apply increase steps conservatively only after performance, drawdown, risk, and operational stability have remained acceptable. Any degradation or risk regression blocks additional scaling.
exit_criteria: Scale-up remains within hard guardrails and approved thresholds
Evidence is reviewed before any increase and is explicitly approved by a human owner
Any degradation in performance, risk, or operational reliability blocks further scaling
No capital increase is permitted as an automatic response to losses or volatility
stages.notes: Capital increases are explicit human decisions, not automatic responses to performance changes.
